said.t: Eight Christians were killed in an attack on St George's Orthodox church in Hamoud, Jordan's deadliest assault on its Christian community since the 1950s.
Jordan's Christian community numbers 250,000 out of 11 million, with Orthodox Christians forming the largest denomination amid a broader climate of sectarian tension.
Friday’s attack on St George's Orthodox church in the village of Hamoud was the largest attack against the country’s Christians since the mid 1950s.
But it faces domestic challenges as its economy has been stagnant for 15 years and the official unemployment rate is 16 per cent.
The kingdom’s Christian population numbers 250,000 out of a population of 11 million.
A shooting at a church in southern Jordan has left seven people dead and 40 injured in a rare and major security incident for the country.
During a press conference later Friday, Jordan's health minister, Ibrahim Al-Bdour, said out of the 40 injured, two remain in critical condition.
Christians make up about 2–3% of the population in Jordan, with sizable communities in the capital Amman, Karak and other parts of the country.
